column2: This workbook is now divided conceptually into business metadata and creative generation direction. Repetition is retained where it is functional; creative cells are individualized.
A template is a composition scaffold, not a finished image prompt. The tracker prompt notes are the page-specific visual story.
Each of the 48 books now has its own subtitle, keywords, short/long description, audience statement, and cover concept.
All 180 pages have page-specific visual direction. Each prompt identifies an action, setting, emotional read, seasonal cue, and representation direction.
The three representation lines now have distinct identity guidance instead of sharing one generic rule set.
Templates now explain composition mechanics while deliberately avoiding generic one-size-fits-all image prompts.
The old repeated workflow note was replaced with a page-specific instruction that points the generator back to the assigned scene.
Pricing, release, bundle, and launch structure remain repetitive where repetition is the actual business logic.
The image program should combine: line identity + season + product theme + page-specific tracker prompt + template structure + global print rules.
If two generated pages look interchangeable, the problem is no longer solved by adding adjectives; revise the page-specific action, composition, props, relationship, or emotional story.
